A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BinaryDM work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original image-generation benchmarks, component ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative results.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, ablations, training-loss measurements and hardware runtime results.

M1.justification: The two-stage EBB, selected application locations, fixed PCA-based LRM and activation quantization remain unchanged. The sign-removal and matrix-update variants are supplementary ablations. The hardware decomposition implements the existing W1A4 computation rather than revising the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, LSUN-Bedrooms, LSUN-Churches, FFHQ and ImageNet under the same conditional and unconditional image-generation tasks. The additions investigate retained coverage rather than introducing datasets or generation tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ReActNet, INSTA-BNN and BI-DiffSR to the W1A4 LSUN-Bedrooms comparison, substantially broadening direct binary-model competition. New Table 17 also evaluates a High-Order comparator for efficiency. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols include W1A4 component ablations, training-loss measurements at specified iterations, additional EBB application scopes, periodic LRM matrix updates and convolution timing on Snapdragon hardware. Existing generation metrics, evaluation sample counts, training budgets and sampler settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: W1A4 component ablations, EBB/LRM training-loss histories, broader EBB scope testing, removal of the residual sign function and LRM matrix-refresh testing. These add distinct questions beyond v4's coefficient, transition-timing, application-scope and dimensionality-reduction analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added loss histories and runtime point estimates do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original main benchmark scores are retained, but substantial results are added. Table 2 reports FIDs of 10.23, 9.42 and 8.58 for ReActNet, INSTA-BNN and BI-DiffSR, versus the retained BinaryDM 7.74. New ablations report 8.53 for EBB alone at W1A4 and 8.44 without the residual sign. Table 17 adds runtimes of 38174.2, 56657.5 and 176371.0 microseconds/convolution for BinaryDM, High-Order and FP. Duplicate 0/0 scope labels in Tables 9–10 leave one added condition ambiguous.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an explicit algebraic decomposition of signed 4-bit activations into four binary components and a bias in Eq. 19. Existing EBB/LRM mathematics is retained; the change from mu to tau in Eq. 9 is notation rather than a revised objective.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same EBB/LRM contributions, first-binarization claim, accuracy claims and headline 15.2-fold OPs and 29.2-fold storage savings. Additional evidence supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes the no-sign variant's poorer optimization to residual-term dominance and incomplete scaling-factor decay. The efficiency discussion also identifies deployment-library and hardware constraints behind measured speedups falling below theoretical OPs savings. The original fixed-projection stability rationale is retained.

D1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 explicitly state typical EBB and LRM coefficients of 0.09 and 0.0001; v4 already included 0.09 in its coefficient sweep. Appendix B.2 adds Larq, Snapdragon 855 Plus and W1A4 implementation details. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing training settings.

R1.justification: v5 adds references including INSTA-BNN, BI-DiffSR, MPQ-DM and additional diffusion and quantization work, while removing references including BRECQ, QDrop, differentiable soft quantization and TFMQ-DM. The broad research positioning remains unchanged; the additional Q-DM bibliography entry represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. Changes include local wording and notation edits, explanatory appendix paragraphs, acknowledgments and the conference-publication header. The expanded appendix introduces repetitive prose and unresolved citation placeholders.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation expands substantially through new ablation, loss-history, update-frequency and runtime tables. Table 2 gains comparator rows, and the EBB scope display changes from checkmarks to numerical counts with an additional loss-history table. Existing figures are unchanged; several original appendix tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v5 better supports the existing contribution through direct binary competitors, W1A4 component evidence and measured hardware efficiency, addressing gaps in v4's validation. The gain is limited by ambiguous EBB scope labels, unresolved citations and runtime evidence confined to convolution-level measurements rather than end-to-end generation. The core method, benchmark coverage and original performance remain unchanged.
